The match was played on 17 April 2021 at the [[Estadio de La Cartuja]] in [[Seville]] between [[Athletic Bilbao]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/05/football/1580911629_748235.html|title=Official: La Cartuja stadium in Seville to host Copa del Rey finals until 2023|website=as.com|publisher=AS|date=5 February 2020|access-date=5 March 2020|archive-date=12 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412184505/https://en.as.com/en/2020/02/05/football/1580911629_748235.html|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2021/01/28/60133312268e3e3e2f8b4576.html|title=The 2020 Copa del Rey final will be played on April 3 and 2021 final on April 17|date=28 January 2021|website=marca.com|publisher=Marca|access-date=3 March 2021}} Barcelona won the match 4–0 for a record-extending 31st Copa del Rey title.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56779320|title=Lionel Messi scores twice as Barca win Copa del Rey final|website=BBC Sport|date=17 April 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}}{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/17/messi-stars-as-barcelona-thrash-athletic-bilbao-to-lift-copa-del-rey |title=Messi stars as Barcelona thrash Athletic Bilbao to lift Copa del Rey|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=17 April 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}} ==Background== The tournament was played amidst the backdrop of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]] which resulted in no crowds being allowed to be present in the stadiums. Barcelona's progress was characterised by narrow victories and dramatic comebacks, including being taken to extra time by part-time neighbours [[UE Cornellà|Cornellà]] after failing to score from two penalties,{{Cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/01/21/football/1611254649_290620.html|title=Cornellà 0-2 Barcelona, Copa del Rey: result, summary and goals|date=22 January 2021|publisher=Marca|access-date=4 March 2021|archive-date=2 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302092740/https://en.as.com/en/2021/01/21/football/1611254649_290620.html|url-status=dead}} finding the net twice in the last 20 minutes to overcome second-tier [[Rayo Vallecano]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55835673|title=Rayo Vallecano 1–2 Barcelona|date=27 January 2021|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=4 March 2021}} and recovering from a 2–0 deficit with just three minutes remaining against [[Granada CF|Granada]], taking the tie to extra time which ended in a 5–3 victory.{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12208129/granada-3-5-barcelona-late-drama-as-barca-win-eight-goal-thriller-to-reach-copa-del-rey-semi-finals|title=Granada 3-5 Barcelona: Late drama as Barca win eight-goal thriller to reach Copa del Rey semi-finals|date=4 February 2021|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|access-date=4 March 2021}} They gave themselves a mountain to climb once again in the semi-final against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] (a repeat of a recent final in [[2018 Copa del Rey final|2018]] and the only round of the competition with two legs), going down 2–0 at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium]]. In the return at [[Camp Nou]], [[Ousmane Dembélé]] scored early and [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] saved a penalty to keep ''Barça'' hopes alive, but they were still behind with 90 minutes played; [[Gerard Piqué]] equalised in the fourth and last minute of [[stoppage time]] to level the tie on aggregate, and in extra time [[Martin Braithwaite]] found the winner to take his side into their 42nd final.{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/mar/04/barcelona-sevilla-copa-del-rey-semi-final-second-leg-match-report|title=Barcelona stun Sevilla with comeback to end awful week in Copa del Rey final|date=3 March 2021|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=4 March 2021}} Athletic Bilbao's route to the event was comparably uncertain: they came from behind to overcome third-level [[UD Ibiza|Ibiza]] 2–1 with a last-minute goal,{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-espana.net/2021/01/21/athletic-bilbao-break-more-hearts-with-a-last-minute-victory-at-ud-ibiza|title=Athletic Bilbao break more hearts with a last-minute victory at UD Ibiza |date=21 February 2021|website=Football Espana|access-date=5 March 2021}} required a late winner again against [[CD Alcoyano|Alcoyano]] (who had eliminated [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] from the competition),{{Cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/teams/athletic-club/2020-21/matches/1_6076/chronicle|title=Athletic Club through to Copa del Rey quarter-finals|date=28 January 2021|website=athletic-club.eus|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|access-date=5 March 2021}} and scored in the third minute of second-half stoppage time minute to take their quarter-final against [[Real Betis]] to extra time, before advancing with a perfect conversion rate in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].{{cite web|url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2021/02/04/athletic-defeats-betis-in-shootout-to-reach-copa-semifinals/115439476/|title=Athletic defeats Betis in shootout to reach Copa semifinals|date=4 February 2021|publisher=[[USA Today]]|access-date=5 March 2021}} In the semi-finals against [[Levante UD|Levante]] they fell behind in both legs but found an equaliser (through [[Iñigo Martínez]] in the first match and a [[Raúl García (footballer, born 1986)|Raúl García]] penalty in the return) to again force extra time; the winner came from a deflected [[Álex Berenguer]] shot with eight minutes of the extended period remaining,{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56288195|title=Levante 1–2 Athletic Bilbao|date=4 March 2021|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=5 March 2021}} reaching the final for the 39th time (one back in [[1904 Copa del Rey|1904]] was never played and the cup awarded to the [[Bilbao]] side in a [[walkover]]). At the time of the clubs qualifying for the 2021 event, the [[2020 Copa del Rey final]] between Athletic Bilbao and [[Real Sociedad]] was still to be played, with its rescheduled date of 3 April 2021 giving the [[Biscay]] club a unique opportunity to win the competition twice inside a fortnight{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56541183|title=Athletic Bilbao: Basque club facing two Copa del Rey finals in two weeks|first=Alex|last=Bysouth|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 April 2021|access-date=5 March 2021}} The delay also meant their current head coach [[Marcelino García Toral|Marcelino]] was the most recent manager to win the competition, having defeated Barcelona in the [[2019 Copa del Rey Final|2019 final]] while in charge of [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. That was the sixth consecutive final for the ''Blaugrana'', and the first defeat for the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] since [[2014 Copa del Rey final|2014]]; the sequence of finals is an outright record and the run of wins is a shared record along with Real Madrid in the 1900s and Athletic in the 1930s. When the 2020 final was eventually played, Athletic fell to a 1–0 defeat.{{Cite news|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=3 April 2021|title=Real Sociedad beat Athletic to claim Copa del Rey and Basque glory|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/03/athletic-bilbao-real-sociedad-copa-del-rey-2020-final-match-report|access-date=4 April 2021|issn=0261-3077}} Barcelona and Athletic Bilbao had played each other in eight previous finals of the tournament; Barcelona won in [[1920 Copa del Rey Final|1920]], [[1942 Copa del Generalísimo|1942]], [[1953 Copa del Generalísimo|1953]], [[2009 Copa del Rey final|2009]], [[2012 Copa del Rey final|2012]] and the most recent in [[2015 Copa del Rey final|2015]], and Athletic in [[1932 Copa del Rey Final|1932]] and [[1984 Copa del Rey Final|1984]].{{cite web|title=Spain - List of Cup Finals|website=[[RSSSF]]|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spancuphist.html|access-date=5 March 2021}}[https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2103282/the-eight-previous-cup-finals-between-fc-barcelona-and-athletic-club/amp The eight previous cup finals between FC Barcelona and Athletic Club], FC Barcelona, 14 April 2021 Their 2021 meeting made the fixture the most played in the history of Copa Del Rey finals, breaking a tied record with [[El Viejo Clásico|Athletic v Real Madrid]]{{refn|group=note|Athletic's website claims they have met Real Madrid nine times,{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/03/23/real-sociedad-our-16th-different-copa-final-opponent/|title=Real Sociedad, our 16th different Copa final opponent |website=athletic-club.eus|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=23 March 2021|access-date=23 March 2021}} but this includes the [[1902 Copa de la Coronación final]], the status of which is disputed both as a Copa del Rey event and as a tournament entered by their club.}} (the third pairing of the trio, ''[[El Clásico]]'' between Madrid and Barcelona, had been played seven times at that point). The sided had also met frequently in [[Supercopa de España]] finals; indeed all of Athletic's four appearances ([[1983 Supercopa de España|1983]], [[2009 Supercopa de España|2009]], [[2015 Supercopa de España|2015]] and [[2021 Supercopa de España final|2021]]) in that competition were against Barcelona. The most recent of these was exactly three months prior to the Copa del Rey final and played at the same venue ([[behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] due to the pandemic), with Athletic winning 3–2 after extra time to claim the trophy with a winning goal from [[Iñaki Williams]].{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/barcelona-vs-athletic/cronica/2021/01/17/6004bcd422601d7c438b4632.html|title=Williams sinks Barcelona and Athletic claim the Supercopa|newspaper=Marca|first=Arch|last=Bell|date=17 January 2021|access-date=5 March 2021}} By reaching the Copa del Rey final, both teams were assured qualification for the four-team [[2022 Supercopa de España]], giving Athletic the chance to defend their title. In the [[2020–21 La Liga]] meetings between the clubs (both played in January 2021 due to scheduling issues, two weeks either side of their Supercopa match), ''Barça'' had the edge with two wins (3–2 at [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés]], 2–1 at Camp Nou, [[Lionel Messi]] scoring three of the goals) though the close scorelines in all three matches demonstrated the narrow margins between the
